tools.name: countersign_stamp
tools.description: Use when you need a signed check, by code that did not make the work, of work you or another agent produced (a report, calculation, summary, filing draft or code) before relying on it or handing it on. Countersign re-computes arithmetic, looks up quotes and values in the cited sources, opens links and parses code, then returns a signed stamp (pass, fail or inconclusive) saying exactly what is wrong, with time and method. The stamp is kept in a public log. No AI model decides the result. It never checks work it produced. Free daily quota; credit keys from $1 at llpro.ai/pay/credit; x402 accepted. Send the key as Authorization: Bearer <llk_ key>. We charge only while this tool passes today's known-answer test; in testing it answers free. Docs: https://llpro.ai/countersign

output.description: The work to check, as text (max 100000 chars). Equations written as '12 * 4 = 48' are re-computed.

producer.description: Who made the work: {agent_id, model}. Required; used for the independence rule.

claims.description: Optional explicit items: {type:'arithmetic', expression, claimed} or {type:'quote', source_url, quote} or {type:'value', source_url, value}

language.description: For code: python or json get a syntax check

private.description: If true the public log shows only a hash of each finding's detail; you still get the full detail

tools.name: countersign_verify
tools.description: Confirm that a Countersign stamp someone shows you is real before you trust it. Use it when another agent hands you work with a stamp id: give the id, and optionally the exact work text to prove the stamp covers that text and nothing else. Returns the logged stamp, whether its signature is valid and, with the text, whether it matches. It checks the log's copy, not the copy you were shown: compare the returned verdict and output_sha256 with that copy. Free, read-only; it does not re-check the work itself.

id.description: Stamp id: the id field of a Countersign stamp

output.description: Optional: the exact work text the stamp should cover; its sha256 is compared with the stamp

tools.name: countersign_log
tools.description: Read the public, append-only log of Countersign stamps: entries after a sequence number, in order, plus the head hash, entry count and public key so you can check signatures yourself. Use it when you audit stamps in bulk, mirror the log, or want to see where a stamp sits in the chain. Free, read-only; private stamps show only a hash of each finding's detail.

after.description: Return entries with a sequence number above this (default 0 = from the first entry)

Free daily quota; credit keys from $1 at llpro.ai/pay/credit; x402 accepted. Send the key as Authorization: Bearer <llk_ key>. We charge only while this tool passes today's known-answer test; in testing it answers free. Docs: https://llpro.ai/countersign

tools.name: certified_lookup
tools.description: LLPRO Certified public register lookup. Send a subject id (a product, service or agent id, lowercase letters, digits, . _ : -, up to 96 characters) to get issued, not_found, revoked or expired for it; send nothing to get the whole register (counts, head hash, criteria hash and the events, up to 200). Every answer is signed by LLPRO Certified (Ed25519 over canonical JSON); check it offline with the verifier at https://llpro.ai/certified-verify. At launch the register holds 0 issued: nothing is certified until a real assessment passes all written criteria. It does not show that a product is safe, legal or fit for any purpose, and not_found does not mean a product failed an assessment. Free. No network, no model, nothing about you is stored on disk.

subject.description: Subject id to look up. Leave out to get the whole signed register.

tools.name: agent_identity_check
tools.description: Does this agent's card agree with the domain that served it and the keys that domain publishes? Send an agent card URL (https) or a domain. We read the card through a safe fetcher and check: required fields; that the domain the card names is the host it was served from; that the operator publishes the same agent id or key at a well-known path on that domain (/.well-known/agent-identity.json or the JWKS); and that a key proves control (the card's own JWS signature, or a signed challenge: a key a card only names, without proof, gives cannot_tell). Get back matches, does_not_match or cannot_tell, every check listed, signed by LLPRO with the time we looked. Shows control of a domain and a consistent card, NOT who the operator is in law, NOT legal identity, NOT safety. It does not show that the agent does what it says, that the domain is not hijacked or the key not stolen, or anything before the time we looked. Not a certification and not a guarantee. Free. Your card address and challenge are not stored; no model. Feeds Identity and payment rails: one input to a decision to deal with an agent, never the whole decision. Limits: public https hosts only (port 443, ASCII domain names), one JSON card up to 200,000 characters, at most 4 fetches per call (a domain tries two card paths). Fetches with the user agent 'Countersign/1.0 (checker; LLPRO)'; robots.txt is not read.

card_url.description: https URL of the agent card, for example https://example.com/.well-known/agent-card.json. Give this or domain.

domain.description: A bare domain such as example.com; we try /.well-known/agent-card.json then /.well-known/agent.json.

challenge.description: Optional proof you hold the key: sign the text 'llpro-agent-identity-check/v1', a newline, the domain, a newline, your nonce, a newline and the time (UTC like 2026-11-12T09:00:00Z, within 10 minutes of now) with the agent's Ed25519 key.

tools.name: witness_record
tools.description: Witness a deal event. Send deal_id, party_id, event_type, content_hash (SHA-256 hex of the content, never the content), your Ed25519 public_key and your sig (base64 signature over the canonical JSON of {content_hash, deal_id, event_type, party_id, type:'witness-event', v:1}). Get back a receipt signed by Witness: the time we saw it, its place (seq) in the deal's chain, and the chain hash over the previous receipt. It shows only that this hash was sent by this key and seen at this time, in this order. It does not show the content is true, who the party is, or that nothing else was sent. Stores hashes, types, public keys, signatures and times for 400 days after the deal's last event; never content or addresses. Free.

deal_id.description: Opaque id both parties use for the deal. Use a random one (16+ characters); anyone who knows it can add events to the chain.

party_id.description: Opaque id of the sender. Its key is fixed by its first event in the deal.

event_type.description: Lowercase label such as offer, accept, payment, delivery, confirm.

content_hash.description: SHA-256 of the event content, lowercase hex.

sig.description: base64 Ed25519 signature over the canonical JSON of the event (see description).

tools.name: page_snapshot_signed
tools.description: What did this public web page show, and when? Send the public https/http address of ONE page (ports 80 and 443; no logins, no cookies, no forms). Get back a screenshot (PNG, 1280 px wide, full page up to 4000 px tall), the visible text, the final address after redirects, the HTTP status, and a note signed with LLPRO's own key that ties the screenshot and the text (by SHA-256) to the address and the time, so anyone can check later that this is what our browser saw then. Free, no sign-up, 30 snapshots a day per caller. We keep no copy: save the answer yourself. It does NOT prove the page was true or what other visitors saw (pages differ by place, time and visitor), and the time is our clock, not an independent timestamp authority. The page text and picture are whatever that page showed. The browser identifies itself in its user agent; robots.txt is not read. Docs: https://llpro.ai/signed-page-snapshot

url.description: Public http(s) address of ONE web page.

full_page.description: true (default): the whole page up to 4000 px tall; false: only the first 800 px.

Expert review $5 an item (check_type expert_review), licensed sign-off $25 (check_type licensed_signoff); start with a $2 check, first 3 free. Send one question a person should answer (does this invoice add up, is this document signed, is this the right business). First 3 checks free per agent, then $2 each by x402 at https://llpro.ai/api/v1/human-check. Attach up to 3 files (PNG, JPEG, WebP or PDF, base64). Get the answer with human_check_result, or give a callback_url. Docs: https://llpro.ai/human-check

tools.name: stamp_notice
tools.description: stamp.notice: a dated, signed record that your AI-use notice existed, and was live on your page, at this time. AI rules require a notice before an automated decision or AI interaction (EU AI Act Art 50 from 2 Aug 2026; California CCPA ADMT pre-use notice and Colorado SB 26-189 from 1 Jan 2027; NYC Local Law 144 notice 10 business days ahead). Send notice_text, the rule, and shown_at (the https page where people see it): we fetch the page and record whether the exact text is on it (state seen) or not (state filed). It proves what was shown and when; it does not say the notice meets any law. $0.10 a filing after 3 free a day; looking up by id is free. Docs: https://llpro.ai/mcp/trust

tools.name: stamp_assessment
tools.description: stamp.assessment: a dated, signed record that a written AI risk or impact assessment existed in this exact form at this time, for this system and version. AI rules ask businesses that use AI for important decisions to write and keep such assessments (for example California's CCPA rules on automated decision-making, Colorado's AI law, EU AI Act Art 27 for some deployers of high-risk systems). Send the assessment text (only its hash is kept unless keep_text=true) or its sha256, the system, its version, the rule and the filer; send supersedes (an earlier as_ id from the same filer) to chain versions. It proves what existed and when; it does not say the assessment is complete or meets any law. $0.25 a filing after 3 free a day; looking up by id is free.

tools.name: record_log
tools.description: record.log: an append-only, hash-chained log kept by LLPRO. Each entry gets a sequence number, the time we received it and a hash that covers the previous entry, so no entry can be added, removed or backdated later without breaking the chain. For records of automated decisions and agent actions that rules say must be kept (for example California's rules on automated decision systems, CCPA risk-assessment records, EU AI Act logging). Send log (a name you choose) and entry (text; only its hash is kept unless keep_text=true) or sha256: only the caller who started a log can write to it. Send log_id alone to read the head and check the chain; send id (le_...) to read one entry. Do not put personal data in entries; send a hash instead. $0.01 an entry after 3 free a day; reading is free.

entry.description: The entry text; we hash it.

sha256.description: Or the entry's SHA-256, 64 lowercase hex.

keep_text.description: Keep the entry text in the record (default false: only the hash).

log_id.description: A log id (lg_...) to read its head and verify its chain.

Send explanation, decision_ref (your own reference, not the person's name), rule, filer and sent_via. For a person to confirm it reads plainly, use human_check_ask with the text. It proves what was sent and when; it does not say the explanation meets any law. $0.10 a filing after 3 free a day; looking up by id is free.
